intent_and_evidence: Engines build one tree of TestDescriptor nodes (engine > class > nested class > method > dynamic test); the launcher filters, prunes, visits and executes it without knowing node kinds. Evidence: TestDescriptor.accept visits itself then calls child.accept(visitor); AbstractTestDescriptor holds the children set and findByUniqueId recurses; NodeTestTask creates one child task per child. Transparent variant: leaf vs container is decided by getType().

All post-discovery filters are merged into one Filter by Filter.composeFilters; CompositeFilter implements Filter, holds a list of Filters and combines their FilterResults into one answer (first exclusion wins). Overlaps A3 (same leaf classes seen as strategies).
Selection rules (tag expressions, method-name patterns, custom filters) are interchangeable algorithms behind PostDiscoveryFilter; EngineDiscoveryOrchestrator only calls apply(). Overlaps A2.

JupiterTestDescriptor fixes algorithms in final methods (getExecutionMode, getLegacyReportingName) and in copyIncludingDescendants, which calls the abstract primitive withUniqueId; subclasses override the hooks (getExplicitExecutionMode, getLegacyReportingBaseName, withUniqueId).

AbstractOrderingVisitor.orderChildrenTestDescriptors runs a fixed ordering algorithm (select, wrap, sort, unwrap, merge) and asks the abstract hook shouldNonMatchingDescriptorsComeBeforeOrderedOnes, which ClassOrderingVisitor and MethodOrderingVisitor answer differently.
Discovery progress (launcher/engine discovery started and finished, selector processed, issues) is pushed to registered LauncherDiscoveryListeners that the orchestrator only knows by interface.
User ClassOrderer/MethodOrderer code expects the public ClassDescriptor/MethodDescriptor API; the wrappers expose internal descriptors through it so internal classes never leak to user code.
final HierarchicalTestEngine.execute fixes the run order (executor service, context, collector factory, HierarchicalTestExecutor); JupiterTestEngine only supplies the steps. Overlaps B2.

The template in B1 asks overridable create* methods which objects to use; JupiterTestEngine overrides them to choose a parallel/same-thread executor, its JupiterEngineExecutionContext and its throwable-collector factory. Overlaps B1.
Sequential vs parallel scheduling is swappable behind HierarchicalTestExecutorService; NodeTestTask and HierarchicalTestExecutor only call submit/invokeAll.
How parallelism is computed (FIXED, DYNAMIC from CPU count, CUSTOM user class) is chosen by configuration; each enum constant implements createConfiguration.
The session's launcher is DelegatingLauncher > InterceptingLauncher > DefaultLauncher; each wrapper implements Launcher and forwards, InterceptingLauncher adds LauncherInterceptor around every call.
EngineExecutionOrchestrator stacks independent wrappers (stack-trace pruning, outcome delaying, memory cleanup) on the engine listener; each forwards and adds one behaviour. Also part of Area C.

Engines report with mutable TestDescriptors; ExecutionListenerAdapter implements EngineExecutionListener and forwards to a TestExecutionListener with immutable TestIdentifiers looked up in the TestPlan. Also part of Area C.
During execution NodeTestTask pushes executionStarted/Skipped/Finished to the EngineExecutionListener from the ExecutionRequest, without knowing who listens. Also part of Area C.
Each node's work is packaged as a TestTask object (execute + execution mode + lock) and handed to an executor service that decides when and on which thread to run it.
A TestDescriptor that is not a Node gets a do-nothing Node from NodeUtils.asNode, so NodeTestTask never needs null checks.

Client-side observers (IDE, summary, logging, unique-id file, JFR, stdout capture) register three ways and are notified of the same run events; notifyEach isolates each listener's failure. Different from B8 (engine side).
LauncherSessionListeners are told when a launcher session opens and closes by DefaultLauncherSession.
The order in which listeners are notified is an interchangeable algorithm: IterationOrder.ORIGINAL for started events, REVERSED for finished events, used by notifyEach.
LoggingListener's behaviour is fixed but where log lines go is an injected BiConsumer (java.util.logging via forJavaUtilLogging, or any sink via forBiConsumer).
Tests call the simple TestReporter API; DefaultTestReporter implements it by calling ExtensionContext.publishReportEntry, which turns the map into a ReportEntry event.
StreamInterceptor extends PrintStream, wraps System.out/err, copies every write into a per-thread buffer and still forwards to the original stream (super.write).
EngineExecutionListener.NOOP and LauncherSessionListener.NOOP stand in for 'no listener' so callers never check for null; LauncherSessionListeners returns NOOP for an empty list.
How a @TempDir directory is created is a TempDirFactory chosen from @TempDir(factory) or the configuration; TempDirFactory.Standard is the default.
How a temp directory is deleted is a TempDirDeletionStrategy (IgnoreFailures or Standard) chosen from @TempDir(deletionStrategy) or the configuration and called from Cleanup.run.
For each parameter the context asks every ParameterResolver supportsParameter; exactly one must match and its resolveParameter supplies the value (none or several is an error).
Each ExecutionCondition encapsulates an enable/disable policy; ConditionEvaluator applies all of them and the first 'disabled' wins.
The platform store does not know how to close Jupiter values, so AbstractExtensionContext injects a CloseAction (close AutoCloseable / CloseableResource values).
Extensions use the namespace-scoped ExtensionContext.Store; NamespaceAwareStore implements it on top of the platform NamespacedHierarchicalStore, fixing the namespace and translating exceptions.

A user's @BeforeEach/@AfterEach Method is wrapped as a synthetic extension implementing BeforeEachMethodAdapter/AfterEachMethodAdapter so it runs through the extension ordering. Adapters are lambdas (no named class).
TestWatcher extensions are told each test's outcome and cannot change it; their exceptions are only logged.

Every test/lifecycle/constructor call passes through a chain of InvocationInterceptors built back to front; each handler can proceed(), skip() or wrap the rest of the chain (interceptor-chain variant).

TimeoutExtension.decorate wraps the Invocation in a timeout-aware Invocation that keeps the original as delegate and adds timing around delegate.proceed(); ValidatingInvocation adds a call-once check.
A resolved reflective call (method or constructor + target + arguments) is packaged as an Invocation object so interceptors can run it later, on another thread, or skip it.
